purpose: Clopidogrel helps prevent dangerous blood clots from forming in your blood vessels. It is commonly used after a heart attack, stroke, or if you have had a procedure like a stent placed in your heart. It lowers your risk of having another heart attack or stroke.
how_it_works: Your blood contains tiny cells called platelets that clump together to form clots. Clopidogrel works by blocking a signal that tells those platelets to stick together. This keeps your blood flowing more smoothly and helps prevent clots from forming in your arteries.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is bleeding more easily than usual — for example, you may bruise more easily, bleed longer from a cut, or notice bleeding gums. You may also have an upset stomach or diarrhea. Some people get a skin rash.
warnings: Because this medication thins your blood, any bleeding can be harder to stop. Tell all your doctors and your dentist that you take this medicine before any procedure or surgery. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first — stopping suddenly, especially if you have a stent, can be very dangerous. Avoid taking ibuprofen or aspirin unless your doctor says it is okay. Seek immediate help if you notice unusual or heavy bleeding, blood in your urine or stool, or if you cough or vomit blood.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one 75 mg tablet taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. Some people are given a higher starting dose (300–600 mg) right away in the hospital after a heart attack or stroke. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes.
